tasks.summary: Fixed the blocking Nz finding from S2.review, and all 8 acceptance commands pass. UCanAccess 5.1.8 implements Nz as overloaded functions, which mangle numbers in two ways. Nz(currency or decimal) goes through a NUMERIC overload with scale 0, so 12.34 comes back as 12. Nz(x, 0) comes back as a DOUBLE. I reproduced both on a database I created. The engine now rewrites every Nz whose argument is not text as COALESCE before UCanAccess converts the SQL, so a non-null value comes back unchanged: Nz(x, d) becomes COALESCE(x, d), and Nz(x) inside arithmetic becomes COALESCE(x, 0). This applies both to views and to the statements it runs. Text Nz keeps UCanAccess's own Nz, which already returns a zero-length string for Null. The engine works out which columns are text from the HSQLDB mirror's INFORMATION_SCHEMA. The catalog's sql/ files still hold the Access SQL. A unit that calls Nz with no default is now flagged needs_access_confirmation, and so is any unit that reads one. New tests in toolkit/tests/test_reference.py cover the rewrite on hand-written SQL, the flag, and exact results from currency and NUMERIC(18,4) columns with nulls, including a query on a query shaped like qryPurchaseOrderList. On synthetic seed-1, all 14 qryPurchaseOrderList TotalCost values match a hand computation from the seed CSVs, with cents and type currency. Engagement results: `reference sql` gives 58 ok, 6 needs-params and 1 unsupported, with 8 units needing confirmation (7 before; qryPurchaseOrderList is new). The engagement database was rebuilt with 28 tables, 611 rows and 58 queries, 0 failures. `reference run` gives 61 ok, 3 needs-params, 1 unsupported and 0 failed. The guard is clean. The full `uv run pytest -q toolkit harness` gives 764 passed and 22 skipped. That count includes the uncommitted S2.synth changes in this worktree, which I did not touch.
notes: How Nz now runs on the engine (toolkit.reference.catalog.nz_for_engine, applied by engine.AccessReference before SQLConverter, for views and for statements). (1) Nz(x, d) becomes COALESCE(x, d), unless x is a text column or d is a string literal; those keep UCanAccess's MEMO Nz, which is exact. (2) Nz(x) next to + - * / \ ^ or Mod becomes COALESCE(x, 0), because Access returns Empty, which counts as 0 in arithmetic. (3) Nz(x) used as a value keeps UCanAccess's Nz when x is text, which returns a zero-length string for Null, as Access does in a query. For a non-text x it returns x unchanged and Null stays Null, because a typed engine cannot put '' in a number column. No Northwind query uses that form.

Assumption to confirm in Access (see manual_steps): Nz with no default in a query returns Empty, which counts as 0 inside arithmetic and shows as a zero-length string as a column value. So TotalCost = ExtendedCost + ShippingFee + TaxAmount, with any Null part counted as 0. qryPurchaseOrderList is now needs_access_confirmation: true, and so would be any unit that reads it; none does in this model.

Goldens must be re-recorded (S2.golden, then the harness) for these units: qryPurchaseOrderList (TotalCost was rounded to whole units and is now exact; describe gives currency), and qryProductList and qryProductList_Export. The two product lists' app-function rewrites use Nz(subquery, 0), which UCanAccess returned as DOUBLE; COALESCE now types it from the subquery, so integers come back as integers. No golden file was edited by this task.
No change to toolkit/reference/bridge.py, build.py, commands.py, qbe.py, toolkit/commands/reference.py or the function rewrite files. The catalog keeps the Access SQL, with Nz, in out/reference/sql/.

Related engine limit, not triggered here: UCanAccess's IIf has String, Integer, Double, Boolean and Timestamp overloads but no BigDecimal one. An IIf that returns currency values would lose exactness the same way. Northwind's IIf calls return datetimes only, so nothing changes now; a later engagement may need the same COALESCE/CASE treatment.

Synthetic seeds rebuilt (3 databases, 84 tables, 3090 rows, 174 queries, 0 failures). Seed-1 run: 59 ok, 2 empty, 3 needs-params, 1 unsupported, 0 failed. Seed-1 qryPurchaseOrderList: 14 of 14 TotalCost values match a hand computation from the seed CSVs, all with cents.
S2.synth answer noted: the SystemSettings tax-rate settings take numeric values in every seed. This task does not depend on it.

The worktree also has uncommitted changes in toolkit/synth.py, toolkit/commands/synth.py, toolkit/tests/test_synth.py and toolkit/tests/fixtures/synth/. They belong to another task (S2.synth); this task did not touch them.

tasks.summary: I fixed the CRLF defect both reviewers found. synth now writes a `.gitattributes` file containing `* -text` into each seed-N/input/ directory, and `--check` compares that file byte for byte with the other dataset files. With it in place, git stores the input CSVs unchanged: the CRLF record ends, and the CR LF inside some seed-2 fields. `git check-attr` on the target repo's input files now shows text unset. The regenerated table bytes and their sha256 values are the same as in attempt 1 (for example seed-2 Products is still 52acff08…e1), so the seed expected goldens stay valid. Three new tests cover this, and test_synth.py now has 33 tests, all passing. One test commits seed 2 into a repo set to `* text=auto eol=lf`, clones it, and checks that the clone matches what synth wrote byte for byte and passes `dataset validate`. Without the file, the same clone differs. The other two tests make `--check` fail when the file is missing or wrong. All 8 acceptance commands passed. Each seed has 28 tables and 1030 rows; `--check` found 0 differences; the guard checked 591 files and found 0 failures.
notes: The git index in the target repo still holds the attempt-1 blobs, which were stored with LF endings (`git ls-files --eol` shows i/lf w/crlf attr/-text). When integrate stages northwind/goldens/synthetic/seed-*/input/, including the new .gitattributes files, git will store the CRLF bytes from the working tree. To be sure every file is re-hashed, it can run `git add --renormalize` on those paths. After the commit, `git ls-files --eol` should show i/crlf for the input CSVs.
The regenerated table bytes and their sha256 values match attempt 1, so the seed-N/expected goldens recorded on these inputs do not need to be recorded again because of this fix.
The synth .gitattributes uses the same `* -text` rule as golden record's file in expected/, with its own header comment. It is written by synth.write_seed, so tests and --check both cover it.
SystemSettings tax-rate settings already get numeric values in every seed (the summary line 'typed values per key: SystemSettings.SettingValue'), as the S2.synth answer asked.

issues.problem: After the Nz-to-COALESCE fix, the engine now reports the ProductToSell column as decimal. qryProductList.ToSell and qryProductList_Export.'Inventory To Sell' were longinteger before. The app function returns a VBA Integer, so Access would give a whole number, but the golden now records it as decimal (for example '26.0000' instead of '26'). Under this type a fractional value would also be accepted where Access cannot produce one. This contradicts the builder's note that 'COALESCE now types it from the subquery, so integers come back as integers'. The values are correct: an independent recomputation matches all 50 seed-1 rows.
issues.evidence: A Python script compared the column types in the working-tree goldens/manifest.json with `git show HEAD:northwind/goldens/manifest.json` in the target repo (exit 0). It printed 'qryProductList ToSell longinteger -> decimal' and 'qryProductList_Export Inventory To Sell longinteger -> decimal'. /home/cloudcli/sourcecode/access-excel-to-django/northwind/goldens/synthetic/seed-1/expected/qryProductList.csv row 2 has ToSell '26.0000'. /home/cloudcli/engagements/northwind-demo/private/out/model/code/modInventory.txt line 355 declares ProductToSell to return Integer. The sibling columns NoStock, Allocated and QuantityOnOrder stay longinteger.

issues.problem: In seed-1, the report window (three months before the latest order date up to that date) contains only orders that have no detail lines. As a result, qryrptSalesByEmployee has 2 rows on seed-1, both with OrderTotal NULL, and qryrptSalesByProduct_ByMonth and qryrptSalesByProduct_ByQuarter are empty. Seed-1 therefore never tests a non-null report total or the Format 'q-yyyy' quarter path. Only seeds 2 and 3 cover them. A hard-coded or wrong aggregation in the sales reports would still pass the seed-1 cell.
issues.evidence: /home/cloudcli/sourcecode/access-excel-to-django/northwind/goldens/synthetic/seed-1/expected/qryrptSalesByEmployee.csv: both data rows have OrderTotal '\N'. `mp-data --slot s2_review_r1_round1 golden record ... --dataset all --check` (exit 0) reports seed-1.empty 2 (qryrptSalesByProduct_ByMonth and qryrptSalesByProduct_ByQuarter). An independent csv recomputation over seed-1/input confirms 0 rows for both and 2 all-null rows for qryrptSalesByEmployee. Only 29 of the 50 seed-1 orders have detail lines.

issues.problem: On redacted runs, the Redactor keeps any skip reason that starts with 'not-implemented: ' and has no newline. It does not check that the runner issued that skip. If app or adapter code calls pytest.skip('not-implemented: ' + <cell value>) on an engagement unit, that value would reach the terminal, the -rA summary and the JUnit message. The runner already records its own not-implemented skips in Runner.not_implemented (nodeid -> unit_id), so the check could require the reason to equal exactly NOT_IMPLEMENTED + that unit id. The canary test does not cover this path.
issues.evidence: harness/redact.py lines 68-75 (`if not reason.startswith(NOT_IMPLEMENTED) or "\n" in reason:` is the only filter); harness/plugin.py lines 434-435 record the runner's own skips in self.not_implemented, but redact() never consults them; harness/tests/test_redact.py has no case where adapter code raises a skip itself. The vendored copy northwind/equivalence/redact.py is identical.

issues.problem: Seed 1 has no rows for 2 kept report units, qryrptSalesByProduct_ByMonth and qryrptSalesByProduct_ByQuarter, so the harness never checks them on that seed. qryrptSalesByEmployee uses the same report-date window and returns 2 rows on seed-1, so seed-1's orders in the last 3 months appear to have no OrderDetails. This lowers the coverage-adjusted rate to 0.9877, and on seed-1 an implementation that hard-codes an empty result for these units would go undetected. Seeds 2 and 3 do cover both units, so no deliverable fails.
